text: Ἀαρών (Hebr.), Aaron, son of Amram and Jochebed, younger brother of Moses.
gloss: Aaron, son of Amram and Jochebed, younger brother of Moses

text: Ἀβαδδών (Hebr.), Destroyer (i. e. Destroying Angel) or ‘place of destruction’ (personified).
gloss: Destroyer (i. e. Destroying Angel) or ‘place of destruction’

text: ἀβαρής, unburdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon.
gloss: unburdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon

text: ἀββά (ἀββᾶ) (Aramaic) (voc.), Father!
Ἅβελ (Hebr.), Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain.
gloss: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain

text: Ἀβιά (Hebr.), Abijah, founder of the eighth class of priests (1 Chron. xxiv 10).
gloss: Abijah, founder of the eighth class of priests

text: Ἀβιάθαρ (Hebr.), Abiathar, a priest in King David's time.
gloss: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time

text: Ἀβιούδ (Hebr.), Abiud, son of Zorobabel and father of Eliakim.
gloss: Abiud, son of Zorobabel and father of Eliakim

text: ἄβυσσος (ἡ), the abyss, the unfathomable depth, an especially Jewish conception, the home of the dead and of evil spirits.
Ἅγαβος, Agabus, a Christian prophet (Ac. xi 28, xxi 10).
ἀγαθοεργέω (ἀγαθουργέω), I work that which is good, I perform good deeds.
gloss: I work that which is good, I perform good deeds

text: ἀγαθοποιία, the doing of that which is good.
gloss: the doing of that which is good

text: ἀγαθοποιός (adj. as noun), a doer of that which is good (ἀγαθοποιῶν gen. pl. masc., 1 Pet. ii 14) (opp. κακοποιός).
gloss: a doer of that which is good

text: ἀγαθουργέω (contracted form of ἀγαθοεργέω, which see).
gloss: contracted form of ἀγαθοεργέω, which see
note: left out of the quiz by David, 2026-11-11

text: ἀγαθωσύνη, (intrinsic) goodness (especially as a personal quality), with stress on the kindly (rather than the righteous) side of goodness.
ἀγαλλίασις, wild joy, ecstatic delight, exultation, exhilaration.
gloss: wild joy, ecstatic delight, exultation, exhilaration

text: ἄγαμος, unmarried, not married, of a person not in a state of wedlock, whether he or she has formerly been married or not.
ἀγανακτέω, I am angry, I am incensed.
gloss: I am angry, I am incensed

text: ἀγανάκτησις, feeling of anger, vexation.
Ἅγαρ (Hebr.), Hagar, the servant of Sarah, wife of Abraham, and interpreted by Rabbinic lore, countenanced by Paul, as a type of Mt. Sinai, where the Mosaic Law was given (Gal. iv 24–5).
gloss: Hagar, the servant of Sarah, wife of Abraham

text: ἀγγαρεύω (from a Persian word, meaning to impress for the postal service), I impress (into my service), I send (on an errand).
gloss: I impress (into my service), I send (on an errand)

text: ἀγγεῖον, a vessel, flask, can.
ἀγγελία, a message.
ἀγγέλλω, I report, I announce (as messenger).
ἄγγος, a vessel.
ἀγέλη, a herd.
ἀγενεαλόγητος, unprovided with a genealogy, whose descent cannot be traced.
gloss: unprovided with a genealogy, whose descent cannot be traced

text: ἀγενής, literally, without γένος (family); hence ignoble.
ἁγιότης, holiness (see ἅγιος), as an abstract quality.
ἁγιωσύνη, the resulting state of the ἅγιος, holy or sanctified state.
gloss: the resulting state of the ἅγιος, holy or sanctified state

text: ἀγκάλη, an arm, especially as bent to receive a burden.
gloss: an arm, especially as bent to receive a burden

text: ἄγκιστρον, a fish-hook.
ἄγκυρα, an anchor.
ἄγναφος, (of cloth) unfulled, unmilled, not yet dressed (by the fuller).
gloss: (of cloth) unfulled, unmilled, not yet dressed

text: ἁγνεία, purity, chastity.
ἁγνισμός, (ceremonial) purification.
ἀγνόημα, an offence committed through ignorance, an error due to (wilful or culpable) ignorance.
ἄγνοια, ignorance, inadvertence; sometimes with the idea of wilful blindness (Eph. iv 18).
ἁγνότης, purity, chastity.
ἁγνῶς, purely, with pure motives, honestly.
ἀγνωσία, disgraceful ignorance.
ἄγνωστος, unknown, unknowable.
ἀγοραῖος, (a) a lounger in the market-place, perhaps with the idea of agitator, Ac. xvii 5; (b) ἀγοραῖοι (understand ἡμέραι), market days; or (understand σύνοδοι, conuentus) assizes.
ἄγρα, catching, a catch.
ἀγράμματος, unlettered, illiterate, uneducated, perhaps with the narrower idea, unacquainted with Rabbinic teaching.
note: 'illiterate' is partly blotted on the image; reading inferred | approved by David, 2026-11-09

text: ἀγραυλέω, I spend the night in the open, bivouac.
gloss: I spend the night in the open, bivouac

text: ἀγρεύω, I catch, capture.
ἀγριέλαιος, a wild olive.
ἄγριος, wild.
ἀγρυπνέω, I am not asleep, I am awake; especially I am watchful, careful.
gloss: I am not asleep, I am awake

text: ἀγρυπνία, the state of being awake (at night).
gloss: the state of being awake (at night)

text: ἀγωγή, leading; hence, mode of life, conduct.
ἀγωνία (properly the feeling of the athlete before a contest), great fear, terror, of death; anxiety.
ἀγωνίζομαι, I am struggling (as in an athletic contest or warfare); sometimes with the object ἀγῶνα expressed.
gloss: I am struggling (as in an athletic contest or warfare)

text: Ἀδάμ (Hebr.), Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race: ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδάμ, its latest ideal representative, who inaugurates the new age, Jesus the Messiah (1 Cor. xv 45).
gloss: Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race

text: ἀδάπανος, without expense, for which nothing has to be paid.
gloss: without expense, for which nothing has to be paid

text: Ἀδδεί (Hebr.), Addei, son of Cosam, and father of Melchei, one of the ancestors of Jesus (Lk. iii 28).
gloss: Addei, son of Cosam, and father of Melchei

text: ἀδελφότης, brotherhood (in the collective sense), the members of the Christian Church, Christendom.
ἄδηλος, unseen, inconspicuous, indistinct (also of sound).
ἀδηλότης, the quality of being unseen (of disappearing), indefiniteness, uncertainty.
gloss: the quality of being unseen (of disappearing)

text: ἀδήλως, out of sight, obscurely, inconspicuously; in 1 Cor. ix 26 perhaps=uncertainly, without certain aim.
ἀδημονέω (originally, I am bewildered, from δήμων, knowing, prudent), I feel fear, I lack courage; I am distressed.
gloss: I feel fear, I lack courage

text: ἀδιάκριτος, without dividings of mind, undivided, whole-hearted.
gloss: without dividings of mind, undivided, whole-hearted
note: 'whole-hearted' breaks at the hyphen at line end; hyphen kept as real

text: ἀδιάλειπτος, unceasing, unremitting.
ἀδιαλείπτως, unceasingly, without remission.
ἀδίκημα, (a) a legal wrong, a crime (with which one is charged), a misdeed; (b) a crime against God, a sin (Rev. xviii 5).
ἀδίκως, unjustly.
Ἀδμείν (Hebr.), Admein, son of Arnei, father of Naasson, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Admein, son of Arnei, father of Naasson

text: ἄδολος, unadulterated, pure.
Ἁδραμυντηνός (Ἀδραμυττηνός), belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, NW. Asia Minor.
gloss: belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, NW. Asia Minor
note: headword printed Ἁδραμυντηνός with Ἀδραμυττηνός in brackets

text: Ἁδρίας, the Hadria, a name given by sailors not merely to the Adriatic Sea, to which it properly belonged, but also to the open Mediterranean to the south-east of Italy, to the sea that lay between Malta, Italy, Greece, and Crete.
ἁδρότης, lavishness, lavish generosity.
ἀδυνατέω, of things, to be impossible.
ᾄδω, I sing.
ἀεί (rare in colloquial Greek), always.
ἀετός, an eagle.

ἄζυμος, unleavened, especially in the neut. plur. τὰ ἄζυμα, the unleavened bread, a festival of the Hebrews, held from 15 to 21 Nisan, in commemoration of their deliverance from Egypt: in a moral sense, 1 Cor. v 7–8.
Ἀζώρ (Hebr.), Azor, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Azor, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok

text: Ἄζωτος, Azotus, Ashdod, a coast town of Palestine belonging to the ancient Philistia, and part of Herod's kingdom.
gloss: Azotus, Ashdod, a coast town of Palestine

text: ἀήρ, air, the lower air we breathe.
gloss: air, the lower air we breathe

text: ἀθανασία, immortality, imperishability, freedom from death.
ἀθέμιτος, illegal, unlawful; thus (nefastus) abominable.
ἄθεος, without god, without (the only true) god, godless.
gloss: without god, without (the only true) god, godless

text: ἄθεσμος, lawless, ignoring the (divine) ordinances.
ἀθέτησις, annulment.
Ἀθῆναι, Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece.
gloss: Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece

text: Ἀθηναῖος, Athenian, belonging to Athens.
ἀθλέω, I engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest.
gloss: I engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest

text: ἄθλησις, a struggling (as in an athletic contest).
gloss: a struggling (as in an athletic contest)

text: ἀθροίζω, I gather together, collect.
ἀθυμέω, I lose heart, am despondent.
ἀθῷος (sometimes, unpunished), guiltless, innocent.
αἴγειος, of a goat.
αἰγιαλός, sea-coast, (sandy) beach; shore (of sea or lake), land.
Αἰγύπτιος, Egyptian.
ἀΐδιος, lasting for ever.
αἰδώς (apparently absent from papyri), shame, modesty.
Αἰθίοψ, Ethiopian, Abyssinian.
αἱματεκχυσία, a shedding or pouring forth of blood (in sacrifice).
gloss: a shedding or pouring forth of blood (in sacrifice)

text: αἱμορροέω, I suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood.
gloss: I suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood

text: Αἰνέας, Aeneas, a citizen of Lydda.
αἴνεσις, praise, commendation.
αἰνέω, I praise.
αἴνιγμα, a riddle.
αἶνος, praise.
Αἰνών, Aenon. Eusebius and Jerome place this site 8 (Roman) miles south of Scythopolis near the Jordan.
αἱρέομαι, I choose.
αἵρεσις (originally, choosing, choice), a self-chosen opinion: a religious or philosophical sect.
αἱρετίζω, I choose.
αἱρετικός, disposed to form sects, sectarian, factious.
gloss: disposed to form sects, sectarian, factious

text: αἰσθάνομαι, I perceive.
αἴσθησις, perception.
αἰσθητήριον, perceptive faculty.
αἰσχροκερδής, fond of base gain.
αἰσχροκερδῶς, in a spirit of eagerness for base gain.
gloss: in a spirit of eagerness for base gain

text: αἰσχρολογία, filthy speech, foulmouthedness.
αἰσχρός, base, disgraceful.
αἰσχρότης, baseness.
αἰσχύνη, shame; shamefacedness.
αἰσχύνομαι, I am ashamed.
αἴτημα, a request.
αἴτιον (neut. of adj. αἴτιος), cause shading into crime; guilt, criminality.
αἴτιος (adj.), the cause of, the originator of; responsible for.
gloss: the cause of, the originator of

text: αἰτίωμα, a charge, accusation.
αἰφνίδιος, sudden.
αἰχμαλωσία, captivity: Hebraistically = captives, Eph. iv 8.
αἰχμαλωτεύω, I take captive (in war).
αἰχμαλωτίζω, I take captive (in war), I subdue, I ensnare.
gloss: I take captive (in war), I subdue, I ensnare

text: αἰχμάλωτος, a captive (in war), hence generally.
ἀκαιρέομαι, I am without a suitable opportunity (to effect something).
gloss: I am without a suitable opportunity (to effect something)

text: ἀκαίρως, unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely.
gloss: unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely

text: ἄκακος, innocent, guileless; simple, Rom. xvi 18.
ἀκάνθινος, made of thorns.
ἄκαρπος, fruitless, profitless.
ἀκατάγνωστος, uncondemned, unimpeachable.
ἀκατακάλυπτος, not veiled, unveiled.
ἀκατάκριτος, uncondemned (probably an attempt to translate the Latin re incognita or causā indictā, ‘(our, one's) case not having been tried’).
ἀκατάλυτος, indissoluble, that cannot be broken up.
gloss: indissoluble, that cannot be broken up

text: ἀκατάπαυστος, not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up), c. gen.
gloss: not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up)

text: ἀκατάστατος (in LXX staggering, reeling), unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic.
ἀκέραιος, (lit. unmixed) simple, unsophisticated.
ἀκλινής, unbent, unyielding, resolute.
ἀκμάζω, I reach maturity, become ripe: I am in full vigour.
ἀκμήν, (properly adverbial acc. of ἀκμή [full time, maturity], and meaning just now) thus, Mt. xv 16 (where parallel in Mk. vii 18 has οὕτως).
ἀκρασία (= ἀκράτεια), incontinence, intemperance (in wide sense).
ἀκρατής, (impotent, hence) lacking self-control, inclined to excess.
ἄκρᾱτος (from κεράννυμι), unmixed, undiluted.
ἀκρίβεια (diligentia), accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.
gloss: accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness

text: ἀκριβής (diligens), careful, accurate, exact, strict, scrupulous, precise.
gloss: careful, accurate, exact, strict, scrupulous, precise

text: ἀκριβόω, I examine carefully, inquire strictly.
ἀκριβῶς (diligenter), carefully, exactly, strictly.
ἀκρίς, a locust.
ἀκροατήριον, auditorium, recitation hall; court room (for hearing cases).
ἀκροατής, a hearer of, a listener to.
gloss: a hearer of, a listener to

text: ἀκρογωνιαῖος (= Attic γωνιαῖος) (adj.), in the corner (of a building), corner-(stone).
gloss: in the corner (of a building), corner-(stone)

text: ἀκροθίνιον (lit. top of a heap), spoil, treasure (taken in war).
ἄκρον (neut. of adj. ἄκρος), edge, tip.
Ἀκύλας, the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila, a male proper name; the husband of Priscilla (Prisca), and a Jew, of a family belonging to (Sinope in?) Pontus.
gloss: the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila

text: ακυρόω, I annul, make of no effect, cancel.
gloss: I annul, make of no effect, cancel
note: no breathing visible on the headword's initial alpha (printed ακυρόω) | approved by David, 2026-11-09

text: ἀκωλύτως (characteristic of legal documents), without let or hindrance.
ἄκων, unwilling, generally used where English would express by an adverb, unwillingly (cf. inuitus).
ἀλάβαστρος, an alabaster phial or bottle.
ἀλαζονεία, arrogant display, ostentation; plur. = occasions of ostentation.
ἀλαζών (gloriosus), boastful, giving one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way.
gloss: boastful, giving one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way

text: ἀλαλάζω (onomatopoeic, cf. Hebrew), I cry aloud, generally of persons (in Mk. v 38 from sorrow): κύμβαλον -άζον, a clanging or clashing cymbal (1 Cor. xiii 1).
ἀλάλητος, unutterable, that baffles words.
ἄλαλος, dumb.
ἅλας (neut.), salt.
ἀλείφω, I anoint.
ἀλεκτοροφωνία (galli cantus, gallicinium), cockcrow, as a period of time, between midnight and 3 a.m.
Ἀλεξανδρεύς, an Alexandrian, a native (or resident) of Alexandria in Egypt.
Ἀλεξανδρινός (or -ῖνος), belonging to Alexandria in Egypt.

Ἀλέξανδρος, Alexander, a proper name of Greek origin, borne by four, possibly five, persons in the N. T., (a) an early Christian, son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried the Cross, Mk. xv 21; (b) a leading non-Christian Jew in Jerusalem, Ac. iv 6; (c) an Ephesian Jew, Ac. xix 33; (d) a renegade Christian at Rome (1 Tim. i 20), probably to be identified with Alexander the coppersmith (2 Tim. iv 14).
gloss: Alexander, a proper name of Greek origin

text: ἄλευρον, meal.
ἀληθεύω, I say (speak) truth, Gal. iv 16; I do truth, I maintain truth (the truth) (see ἀλήθεια for the sense of ‘truth’).
ἀλήθω, I grind.
